author: Adelaar, Alexander
title: Malagasy phonological history and Bantu influence
notes: Consulted directly on 25 November 2026 (Project MUSE PDF in Downloads). A critique of Wolff's (2010) treatment of Malagasy. §2.3 states the changes in three stages: Proto-South East Barito (PSEB1-9, Table 3, p. 131, premigratory, shared with the SEB languages of Kalimantan), Proto-Malagasy (PMLG1-4, Table 4, p. 135, postmigratory) and the dialects (MLG1-4, Table 5, p. 136; Merina MRN1-4, Table 6, p. 138); §3 the spirantization of stops and semivowels, §4 the retroflex affricate tr, §5 the reduction of nasal + stop clusters, §6 PAN *s; §7 Bantu (Sabaki, Comorian) contact. Data sources in the Appendix (pp. 155-156): Maanyan from Dahl (1951), Merina from Webber (1853), Richardson (1885) and Abinal & Malzac, South Sakalava from Gueunier (n.d.), North Sakalava from Thomas-Fattier (1982), Bara from Elli (1988), South Betsimisaraka from Ruud (1955), Old South Betsimisaraka from Flacourt (1658), Old Taimoro (Sorabe script) from Ferrand (1904). Malagasy written in its orthography with o as u, ŋ for the velar nasal, paragogic vowels with a breve and stress marked; PAN and PMP in Blust's ACD notation with ə for *e.
